description: The formal CDSS application process, orientations, and the physical plant inspection for a Residential Care Facility for the Elderly (RCFE).

sections.title: Orientations
sections.summary: Complete the required CDSS training components before final submission.

bullets.label: Complete RCFE Initial Certification Training Program (ICTP)
bullets.detail: The prospective administrator must complete the 80-hour RCFE Certification program, pass the state exam, and clear a criminal background check.

bullets.label: Complete Component I (Online Orientation)
bullets.detail: This provides a general overview of the RCFE licensing process. You must pay the orientation fee, complete the online modules, and save the certificate for your application packet.

sections.title: Part A
sections.summary: Submit the core legal, financial, and operational forms to the Centralized Applications Bureau (CAB).

bullets.label: Application (LIC 200)
bullets.detail: The core application form for a Community Care Facility or RCFE. Must contain original signatures of all applicants or general partners.

bullets.label: Applicant Information (LIC 215)
bullets.detail: Requires original signatures. Reference statements must be current and cannot be provided by relatives.

bullets.label: Designation of Administrative Responsibility (LIC 308)
bullets.detail: Designates the individual(s) authorized to act in the licensee's absence. A licensee cannot designate themselves. Essential for ensuring 24/7 administrative coverage.

bullets.label: Administrative Organization (LIC 309)
bullets.detail: Required if the applicant is a corporation, public agency, partnership, or LLC. Not required for sole proprietorships.

bullets.label: Affidavit Regarding Client/Resident Cash Resources (LIC 400)
bullets.detail: Details whether the facility will handle resident funds. Must contain original signatures.

bullets.label: Surety Bond (LIC 402)
bullets.detail: Required if the facility safeguards resident cash resources. The bond amount must match the amount indicated on the LIC 400.

bullets.label: Monthly Operating Statement (LIC 401)
bullets.detail: Projects all facility operating costs. Salaries must meet minimum wage, and ~25% should be added for fringe benefits unless specifically not applicable.

bullets.label: Supplemental Financial Information (LIC 401a)
bullets.detail: Reflects all other income and expenses outside of the facility income. Required to verify financial solvency.

bullets.label: Balance Sheet (LIC 403)
bullets.detail: Reflects the total assets and liabilities of the owners, encompassing both facility-related and external finances.

bullets.label: Financial Information Release (LIC 404)
bullets.detail: Authorizes CDSS to verify bank accounts and lines of credit. Used to confirm the 3-months of required operating capital.

bullets.label: Facility Personnel Summary Report (LIC 500)
bullets.detail: Details all planned employee positions, including scheduled days and hours, to verify adequate staff coverage.

bullets.label: Personnel Record (LIC 501)
bullets.detail: Submitted to licensing only for the administrator (if not the licensee). Other staff forms are kept on file at the facility.

bullets.label: Health Screening Report (LIC 503)
bullets.detail: Verifies the applicant/administrator is in good health. Must be completed less than 1 year prior to application and include a TB test.

bullets.label: Criminal Record Statement (LIC 508)
bullets.detail: Required for the applicant and the designated administrator to verify background clearance.

bullets.label: Emergency and Disaster Plan for Residential Care Facilities for the Elderly (LIC 610E)
bullets.detail: RCFE-specific disaster plan detailing evacuation routes, emergency contacts, and relocation sites. Relocation sites require written authorization.

bullets.label: Facility Sketch (LIC 999)
bullets.detail: Floor plan showing all rooms, door and window exits, and designated ambulatory/non-ambulatory bedrooms.

bullets.label: Local Fire Inspection Authority Information (LIC 9054)
bullets.detail: Provides CDSS with the contact information for the local fire jurisdiction to initiate the fire clearance process.

sections.title: Part B
sections.summary: Submit the facility's specific operational plans, policies, and procedures.

bullets.label: Partnership Agreement/Articles of Incorporation/Organization
bullets.detail: Establishes the legal framework and ownership structure of the facility, showing who holds ultimate liability and operational responsibility.

bullets.label: Verification of Administrator Qualifications
bullets.detail: A copy of the RCFE Administrator Certificate, resume, and proof of age (must be at least 21 years old) to verify qualifications.

bullets.label: Job Descriptions
bullets.detail: Detailed descriptions of duties and required qualifications for all facility roles, including caregivers, cooks, and activities coordinators.

bullets.label: Personnel Policies
bullets.detail: The facility's rules regarding staff conduct, scheduling, benefits, and disciplinary procedures.

bullets.label: In-service Training for Staff
bullets.detail: The schedule and curriculum for ongoing staff training, including mandatory RCFE topics like dementia care, medication assistance, and postural supports.

bullets.label: Plan of Operation / Program Description
bullets.detail: A comprehensive narrative detailing the facility's purpose, target population (elderly, dementia, etc.), services provided, and daily routines.

bullets.label: Personal Rights
bullets.detail: Documentation outlining how the facility will inform residents of their rights under Title 22, including the use of form LIC 613C-2.

bullets.label: Admission Policies & Agreement
bullets.detail: The criteria for accepting or discharging residents, along with a copy of the contract detailing fees, services, and eviction conditions.

bullets.label: Sample Menu
bullets.detail: A 30-day sample menu demonstrating nutritional compliance with dietary guidelines for the elderly, including accommodations for special diets.

bullets.label: Control of Property
bullets.detail: Proof of the right to operate on the premises, such as a deed, lease agreement, or a signed LIC 311A form from the property owner.

bullets.label: Neighborhood Complaint Policy
bullets.detail: Procedures for receiving, logging, and resolving complaints from surrounding neighbors to maintain good community relations.

bullets.label: Dementia Care Plan (If Applicable)
bullets.detail: If the facility intends to admit residents with dementia, a specialized plan detailing secured perimeters, specific staff training, and tailored activities must be submitted.

sections.title: Pre-Licensing & Fire Clearance
sections.summary: The final inspections to ensure physical safety and compliance before the license is issued.

bullets.label: Request STD 850 (Fire Clearance)
bullets.detail: CDSS will submit this request to the local fire authority. The home must meet strict RCFE fire codes, including interconnected smoke alarms and proper exit pathways for non-ambulatory residents.

bullets.label: Pass the Pre-Licensing Inspection
bullets.detail: An LPA will conduct an on-site walkthrough to verify the home is ready. Note: If the inspection is due to a change of ownership with residents already in care, the LPA will use form LIC 311F to review required file documents.
